draft.title: Newer Small LLMs Seem Better at Coding but Weaker on World Knowledge—Anyone Else Seen This?
draft.body:
I've been reading a 2025 report where the author tested various LLMs on coding, engineering problem solving, and also on world knowledge questions like local history and technical standards. Interestingly, despite newer small models often scoring higher on benchmarks and being promoted as equivalent to older, larger models, their world knowledge appeared worse than that of their bigger predecessors and sometimes even worse than lower-benchmarking models of similar size.

This suggests a tradeoff where newer small models might optimize problem-solving skills at the expense of general knowledge depth.
